Three tasks provide limited evidence for transferable curvature.","falsifying_response":"Adding this feature fails to reduce task-balanced held-out Y prediction error beyond uncertainty under the fixed predictor."},{"name":"removal_directional_level_curvature","expression":"removed_fraction * aligned_level_shift * abs(aligned_level_shift)","measurement_meaning":"Signed counterpart of removal-weighted squared level displacement, allowing different curvature for opposite shift directions.","limitation":"The supplied directional Y differences vary across tasks. Neither a universal coefficient sign nor a causal effect is established; this feature may correlate strongly with the symmetric term.","falsifying_response":"On future held-out tasks, adding this feature to the baseline plus the symmetric term produces no incremental Y error reduction beyond uncertainty, or worsens prediction."}],"reasoning":"The largest supplied quadratic prediction errors include removal actions, whose Y responses show substantial and task-dependent directional asymmetry. These two terms permit removal-dependent symmetric and directional curvature beyond existing quadratic terms without identifiers or fitted thresholds. Z measures target-versus-complement improvement and is not substituted for global Y. These are retrospective candidates; no augmented-model performance has been measured."}
